summary: Re-check expiry on every resolve (evicting the entry), add ShortenerService.createBatch behind POST /api/v1/urls/bulk, extend the create rate limiter to the new path, and add a partial index on expires_at as a new migration.

decisions.title: Check expiry on every resolve
decisions.rationale: CachedLink already holds expiresAt, so the check is one clock read. It is cheaper and simpler than shortening the cache TTL and cannot be defeated by it.

decisions.title: Per-item results for bulk
decisions.rationale: Items are independent, so one bad URL should not fail 99 good ones. The response reports created and rejected counts and a status per item.

decisions.title: Bulk counts as one create for rate limiting
decisions.rationale: Keeps the limiter a simple per-request counter. The per-item cost is not modelled, which is recorded as a risk.

decisions.title: New partial index on expires_at (V3)
decisions.rationale: Supports expiry lookups and a future purge job. Partial because most links never expire. Added as a new migration; V1 is never edited.

intendedFiles.purpose: Enforce expiry on every resolve; add createBatch
Apply the create rate limit to the bulk path too
Replace the test that asserted the defect with regression tests

risks: A bulk request counts as one create, so 100 links per permitted request; per-item cost is not modelled
Batch creation is not atomic by design: a failure part way leaves earlier items created
